requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 must not be able to exchange traffic directly with each other on the shared subnet
requirements.summary: Baseline showed node2<->node3 ping succeeded (cmd-ac8a305ed7ef4924, cmd-11072217ca084454). firewalld rich rules dropping the peer's source IP were applied on both node2 (drop 10.100.80.12) and node3 (drop 10.100.80.11), both at runtime and --permanent (cmd-5746f92ae921406d, cmd-862409c90ee045e2). Post-change verification shows node2->node3 and node3->node2 ping at 100% loss (cmd-82774478121845c2, cmd-eff042f2f5d140a0). Isolation was re-confirmed to survive a firewalld --reload (cmd-2bc91854b99b43e1, cmd-8ecb3db93229438b) and, further, survived independent reboots of node1, node2, and node3 (cmd-03c15c7288484eca, cmd-2656d61c6cbd406c, cmd-e0f3e86508f54317, cmd-f7c4d89784f64027, cmd-6ba9acfef62441dc), all showing continued 100% loss between node2 and node3 with the rich rule still present.

requirements.requirement: Both node2 and node3 must continue to reach node1 on the shared subnet after isolation is applied
requirements.summary: After the rich rules were applied, node2->node1 and node3->node1 pings both succeeded with 0% loss (cmd-82774478121845c2, cmd-eff042f2f5d140a0), and node1->node2/node1->node3 also succeeded confirming bidirectional reachability with node1 (cmd-59d4deb039934c35). This connectivity to node1 was re-verified after each of the three node restarts (cmd-925ffa4e310b4fae, cmd-e0f3e86508f54317, cmd-f7c4d89784f64027, cmd-6ba9acfef62441dc), consistently showing 0% loss to node1 while node2<->node3 remained blocked.

overall_summary: The executor correctly identified the actual shared subnet (10.100.80.0/24, the only addressed interface common to node1, node2, and node3 in the captured evidence) and isolated node2 and node3 from each other using symmetric firewalld rich-rule drops on each host's incoming traffic from the peer's IP, while leaving connectivity to node1 untouched. Isolation was verified before/after application, after a firewalld reload, and after independently rebooting all three nodes (with boot-id changes confirming genuine restarts and full recovery of firewalld state and connectivity/isolation behavior each time). The provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was executed thoroughly and directly corroborates the fixed before/after boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found; only trivial reboot-log residue remains.
limitations: The topology metadata names two per-node networks ('mgmt' and 'seg'), but the evidence shows only one IP-addressed interface (10.100.80.0/24) shared by all three nodes; the executor applied isolation there since it is the only observed shared subnet, which this evaluation treats as the correct interpretation of 'the same segment' referenced in the task, but the seg network's role could not be independently confirmed from evidence.
Package-health checks on node2 and node3 timed out both before and after the executor's work, so package-manager state consistency could not be verified as a cross-check.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the full chronological command trace, the executor's state-changing actions were: firewalld rich-rule additions on node2 and node3 (cmd-5746f92ae921406d, cmd-862409c90ee045e2) directly implementing the task; firewalld --reload on both nodes (cmd-2bc91854b99b43e1, cmd-8ecb3db93229438b) used solely to confirm rule persistence, a bounded and low-risk verification step; and three node reboots (cmd-702e759a375c4a41, cmd-8654f89799fd46a9, cmd-42d1bb0972c44a3c) performed as the mandated provider-wide restart-evidence protocol, each followed by recovery and re-verification. No unrelated or unexplained mutations (package installs, config rewrites, unrelated service changes) were observed. Minor residue: a /tmp/reboot.log file was left on node2 and node3 from the nohup-wrapped reboot commands (visible in after_executor temporary-files diff), a trivial, non-security-relevant artifact of the reboot mechanism itself rather than an unnecessary experiment. All discovery/diagnostic commands (ip, bridge, systemctl, whoami/sudo checks, failed unauthenticated firewall-cmd attempts) were read-only or failed without mutating state.
